thread:
sam: Quick sync — I'm putting together a proposal for differentiated retention for auth and privileged logs. Idea is: keep full detail (IP, raw headers) for 30d, then move to a hashed/metadata-only tier for 1y, and archive stripped records for 7y. Need opinions on SIEM export patterns + how we want KMS unwraps to work for temporary forensic access.

meera: 👍 high-level sounds fine. question: are we treating all privileged-service logs the same as human-auth logs? e.g., service-to-service auth calls probably need shorter full-detail retention.

sam: Good point — thinking to classify by principal type: user, human-admin, service-account. Human-admin = 30d full; user = 14d full; service-account = 7d full, then metadata. But open to pushback.

derek: For SIEM exports, we should avoid exporting raw logs unless there is an explicit request ticket. Proposed pattern: export proxy that only unwraps per-export with ephemeral KMS keys bound to the ticket ID and TTL. That way exported blob is decryptable for N hours.

olivia: I like ephemeral unwrap but we need an RBAC change template so auditors can trace who requested and why. Can we enforce a policy where exports require both a ticket and a 2nd approver for anything >24h TTL?

sam: Yes — add approver gate for >24h. Also want to reduce blast radius: exported artifacts should undergo automated masking for PII (emails, tokens) unless explicit forensics flag is set.

sec-bot: incident-bot detected phrase "export" in this thread — remember to attach a JIRA or CT ticket for any real exports.

meera: Quick practical Q: how do we implement the ephemeral KMS pattern? Is it: create a data key, encrypt with customer CMK? or a proxy that rewraps to a short-lived key?

derek: Implementation sketch: 1) export request -> authorize via OPA + RBAC (ticket id) 2) proxy copies filtered log objects to export bucket encrypted with an ephemeral key (generated and wrapped by our CMK) 3) generate a one-time unwrap token that the approver can use to fetch & decrypt within TTL. We store audit record: ticket id, requester, approver, unwrap-token-id, TTL.

iris: What about legal/forensics hold? We should ensure holds can revoke unwrap tokens and mark exports as immutable. If a legal hold exists, prevent automatic deletion and make exports read-only until cleared.

olivia: Also add requirement: every RBAC change that allows exportable viewable fields must include a justification string and a list of example queries. Internal auditors will want that.

sam: Drafted a tiny snippet of the export config we could use in the proxy. Thoughts?

sam: ```yaml
# export proxy config example
export: 
  ticket_required: true
  approver_required_for_ttl_gt_hours: 24
  mask_default: true
  allowed_principals: ["human-admin", "security-team"]
  ephemeral_key_ttl_seconds: 7200
  audit_store: "kms-wrapped-metadata"
```

derek: Looks good. Suggest adding a field "redaction_profile" so different classes (PCI, PII, General) map to different masking pipelines.

meera: For SIEM feeds (streaming), we need a separate path: aggregated metadata feed vs full-event feed. Full-event feed should be opt-in and restricted to dedicated SIEM consumers with limited retention.

sam: Agree. We'll publish two connector types: metadata-only (default) and full-event (requires contract + 2 approvers + keystore wrap).

olivia: Ops question — who gets permission to create ephemeral keys? We should restrict to a small service account, and require CMK rotation policy. Also document how to rotate without breaking old unwrap tokens (we need key versioning).

iris: On incident response: if we need immediate access during active IR, allow an emergency bypass path that logs to a tamper-evident audit trail and auto-notifies legal + CISO. Keep bypass TTL short (e.g., 1 hour).

meera: For vuln triage, we should tie retention policy decisions back to actual triage needs. E.g., if a vulndb report needs raw header chain for reproduction, we should be able to request timeboxed full-data retrieval and attach to the ticket.

sam: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with: retention matrix by principal, SIEM connector types, export proxy behavior (ephemeral KMS rewrap), RBAC template for export requests, and emergency bypass playbook. Can folks review + add comments by EOD Friday?

derek: I'll add a sequence diagram to show unwrap flow.

olivia: I'll draft the RBAC change template and sample justification language.

iris: I'll run the legal/forensics hold wording by counsel; will comment inline.

meera: I'll map use-cases from vuln triage so we don't over-retain.

sam: Thanks all — posting RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
